robotics_kits_intro: From simple wheeled robots for the first lessons to ESP32 IoT systems and computer vision. Open any kit to see its description, specification and learning outcome.

robotics_kits_list.name: 4-wheel car
robotics_kits_list.gist: A four-wheel-drive multifunction smart car built on Arduino with Bluetooth control. The robot avoids obstacles on its own, follows a line and tracks light sources.
robotics_kits_list.outcome: Students learn how to wire up sensors, program the driving logic and make boards talk to each other over a wireless link. They build algorithms for autonomous vehicle control.
features: Four-wheel drive
Bluetooth and IR remote control
Obstacle avoidance, line following, light tracking
Block-based programming and IDE support
specs: Wireless control: IR up to 10 m, Bluetooth up to 50 m (Android/iOS)

robotics_kits_list.name: 4-wheel car with robotic arm
robotics_kits_list.gist: A four-wheel robotic platform fitted with a movable mechanical gripper. The whole rig is driven remotely from a smartphone.
robotics_kits_list.outcome: Students grasp how servo motors work and how a robotic arm moves through space. They gain hands-on experience building mobile interfaces that drive the car and the gripper at the same time.
features: Four-wheel drive plus a 4 DOF robotic arm
Smartphone control through a mobile app
Grabs, lifts and moves objects
Autonomous driving and obstacle avoidance
specs: Wireless control: IR up to 10 m, Bluetooth 20 – 50 m (Android/iOS)

robotics_kits_list.name: 2-wheel car
robotics_kits_list.gist: A small wheeled learning robot shaped like a turtle, built specifically for STEM classrooms. It carries a basic sensor set: ultrasonic ranging, line following and infrared remote control.
robotics_kits_list.outcome: The kit is a perfect starting point: students pick up basic Arduino syntax and obstacle-avoidance algorithms, and sharpen their logical thinking by solving navigation problems.
features: Learning robot with a round chassis
Line following, obstacle avoidance and IR control
Built-in LED matrix for faces and symbols
Easy assembly and block-based programming
specs: Wireless control: IR up to 10 m, Bluetooth up to 50 m

robotics_kits_list.name: Smart house
robotics_kits_list.gist: An interactive smart-house model that simulates home automation: automatic doors, windows, ventilation and lighting. Every system reacts to its surroundings or is driven remotely.
robotics_kits_list.outcome: Students grasp the Internet of Things and learn to automate everyday processes with gas, flame and motion sensors. They pick up the basics of designing safety and comfort systems.
features: Full smart-home simulation
Automatic doors, lighting and ventilation control
Gas leak, smoke and humidity detection
Control from a mobile app or straight from the sensors
specs: Input voltage: 6 – 9 V or USB 5 V
Maximum current per pin: 20 mA (digital I/O), 50 mA (3.3 V)
Sensors: motion (PIR), gas, temperature and humidity, light

robotics_kits_list.name: Eco house
robotics_kits_list.gist: An eco-minded smart-house model focused on energy efficiency and indoor climate control. The kit supports temperature, humidity and environmental monitoring sensors.
robotics_kits_list.outcome: The kit builds environmental awareness through the lens of modern technology. Students learn to collect analytical data about their surroundings and write algorithms that save resources.
features: Eco house built around renewable energy
Solar energy, temperature and humidity monitoring
Automatic blinds and lighting control
Programming in C/C++
specs: Input voltage: 6 – 9 V (solar panel or batteries)
Actuators: solar panel, servo, solenoid, fan
Sensors: light, soil moisture, rain, temperature

robotics_kits_list.name: Tracked tank
robotics_kits_list.gist: A tracked mini tank that handles rough ground far better than an ordinary wheeled car. It carries sensors for automatic manoeuvring, obstacle detection and path following.
robotics_kits_list.outcome: Students study the mechanics of tracked drive and how motor torque is managed through a turn. They learn to work with more demanding chassis types and to synchronise sensors in real time.
features: Tracked mini tank with high ground clearance
Ultrasonic obstacle avoidance and object following
Built-in LED matrix for visual effects
Bluetooth control
specs: Wireless control: IR up to 10 m, Bluetooth 10 – 20 m

robotics_kits_list.name: Smart steering wheel
robotics_kits_list.gist: A dedicated steering wheel with tilt sensors — an accelerometer and a gyroscope. Connect it to a robot car and the robot obeys the wheel’s movements in the air.
robotics_kits_list.outcome: Students find out how modern motion-recognition systems and spatial sensors work. They get hands-on practice sending telemetry between two separate devices — the wheel and the car.
features: Drive the car by moving the wheel
Wireless data link between wheel and car
Accurate tilt and rotation sensing
Room to program extra car functions

robotics_kits_list.name: Walking robot
robotics_kits_list.gist: A walking robot built on Arduino Nano that moves on servo-driven legs.
robotics_kits_list.outcome: Children meet the basics of bio-robotics and the balancing mechanisms behind walking machines. Block-based programming lets even the youngest students set up the robot’s walk and dance moves.
features: Walking robot with 4 degrees of freedom (4 DOF)
Mimics the hops and gait of living creatures
Control from a graphical app on iOS and Android
Ideal for studying servos and biomechanics
specs: Input voltage: 7 – 12 V (or a 3.7 – 7.4 V battery)

robotics_kits_list.name: Solar station
robotics_kits_list.gist: A smart solar tracker that uses photoresistors to turn the panel after the light source on its own. It also carries a display and a module for charging a phone from the sun.
robotics_kits_list.outcome: Students study renewable energy sources and automatic positioning in depth. They learn to program precise tracking systems driven by the difference between light sensor readings.
features: Two-axis automatic sun tracking
Higher solar panel efficiency
Phone charging over a USB output
Light level data visualisation
specs: Extra: USB output for charging mobile devices

robotics_kits_list.name: Robotic arm manipulator
robotics_kits_list.gist: A desktop acrylic manipulator with four degrees of freedom, driven by two joysticks. The robot is built for picking up, lifting and moving small objects precisely.
robotics_kits_list.outcome: Students gain the fundamentals of industrial automation and coordinate control in space. They learn to coordinate several servos at once so the arm moves smoothly.
features: Desktop robotic arm with a gripper and 4 DOF
Precise gripper positioning with joysticks
Lifts, rotates and grabs light objects
Open source code for custom programs
specs: Degrees of freedom: 4 DOF (base, shoulder, elbow, gripper)
Control: joysticks, potentiometers or mobile app

robotics_kits_list.name: Electronic scale
robotics_kits_list.gist: A kit for building a digital scale with a 5 kg load cell and an analog-to-digital converter. It comes with a matrix keypad, a real-time clock and an LCD that shows the weight and the calculated price.
robotics_kits_list.outcome: Students understand the physics of measuring force and mass electronically, and how sensors are calibrated. They build a genuinely useful household instrument and handle demanding maths in code.
features: Build a working electronic scale up to 5 kg
High-precision weight measurement
Readout on an LCD display
Taring and calibration from code

robotics_kits_list.name: Smart irrigation system
robotics_kits_list.gist: An automated plant watering system. It uses a capacitive soil moisture sensor and a water pump to irrigate on a schedule or whenever the soil dries out.
robotics_kits_list.outcome: Students study closed-loop control systems that run without a human in the loop. They gain practical skills in agritech and in working safely with pumps and liquids around electronics.
features: Automatic plant watering
Real-time soil moisture monitoring
